title: Music in the house: his mother and grandmother
summary: Davison says music was always around him; his mother sang and played piano, and as a baby he pounded pans in time to her playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, the first thing that anybody ever says to you when they want to know something about you, they always say - how did you get started? Well, that's a pretty hard thing to describe; I think music doesn't get started; it happens. And, of course, in my house, from the time I was one year old, there was always music around. My mother was a great vocalist and played very good piano. As a matter of fact she was so good that she used to play the silent movies. Plus the fact that I think she was the only Protestant that ever sang in a Catholic church - that's how good she was. And, I suppose my coming along sort of knocked her career in a top hat because she wanted to go on with her music, but anyway, she said that - how you get started - she said that when she used to play the piano and be playing something that had some type of swing to it at all, that I would--- this is before I was walking she says I did this -- that I used to go in the kitchen where the pans were and get out a pan or two and pound on the pan to the rhythm of her playing. Of course, now, that's what she says, but that - she says - she could tell that I was keeping time with her. That's certainly unusual before you're able to walk. But, I can understand all that because later on, I had a grandmother on my father's side who also gave piano lessons and musical instruments used to fascinate me; just to see a violin or mandolin or a banjo or a guitar or a trumpet or something, I was just fascinated with it, you know.
